title: api: unify rate-limit semantics, idempotency handling, and retry-after header (openai-compat updates)
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: customers observed inconsistent 429/503 semantics across hosted/dedicated/private deployments and divergent Retry-After behavior between Redwood API and our OpenAI compatibility layer. This caused client retry logic and SDKs to behave unpredictably (duplicate processing, streaming interruptions). This PR unifies rate-limit semantics and idempotency handling across the API surface, stabilizes streaming error paths, and updates OpenAI-compat mappings so clients get consistent, documented responses. Summary of changes: 1) Standardized Retry-After semantics: always return HTTP Retry-After (seconds) on 429 and 503 when the server expects throttling/backoff; introduced X-RateLimit-* headers for remaining/limit/reset when available. 2) Idempotency key enforcement: request router now normalizes and validates Idempotency-Key header, routes duplicate requests to a deduplicator service that returns stored response for recent successful requests (TTL configurable by customer tier). 3) Streaming stability: resume-on-retry semantics for chunked streams - when transient 503/429 occurs mid-stream we now send a terminal error frame with standardized code and advisory Retry-After; the SDKs will attempt resume only if an idempotency key was supplied and backend supports KV cache for stream offsets. 4) Error code unification: mapped internal error classes to consistent OpenAI-compat error codes and fields (type, message, param) and added stable error_id for debugging. 5) Backfill and migration: compatibility layer accepts both old and new header shapes during a 28-day co-existence window. 6) Observability: new metrics (rate_limit_denied, idempotency_hit, stream_resume_attempts) and tracing tags. The description below lists files touched, commit summary, review discussion and rollout notes.
commits: Refactor: move rate-limit logic to api/gateway/rate_limiter.go (normalization + X-RateLimit headers)
Feature: deduplicator service and idempotency cache (services/dedup/*) + integration in router
Fix: stabilize chunked streaming paths and add terminal error frames (runtime/streaming/*)
Compat: map internal errors to OpenAI-compatible error envelope (api/compat/openai_mapper.go)
Misc: add metrics and tracing updates, tests and integration harness changes
files_changed_summary: api/gateway/rate_limiter.go - core rate limit decisioning and Retry-After header generation
services/dedup/service.go - in-memory/redis-backed idempotency cache and response replay
runtime/streaming/stream_manager.go - terminal error frames, resume-on-retry hooks
api/compat/openai_mapper.go - mapping internal errors to OpenAI-compatible JSON envelope
sdk/python/openai_compat.py - updated client to honor Retry-After and idempotency resume semantics
docs/api/rate-limits.md - updated semantics and migration notes
review_conversation: Miguel Alvarez (2026-02-22): Left a few nits, main question around dedup TTL default and memory implications for Dedicated customers.
Asha Patel (2026-02-22): Reply - default TTL 24h for hosted, configurable per-tenant for Dedicated/Private; implementation uses Redis LRU to bound memory. Added config and docs note.
Lisa Chen (2026-02-24): Concern - streaming resume requires both idempotency key and server-side stream offset storage; how do we GC offsets?
Asha Patel (2026-02-24): Reply - offsets are stored with the idempotency entry and GC'd with the TTL; added metrics for orphaned offsets and follow-up ticket ENG-1482 to add eviction alerts.
Evan Brooks (2026-02-26): Approve after CI fixes; suggested adding a small compatibility test that hits old header shapes.
Asha Patel (2026-02-27): Added compatibility tests and re-ran CI. Ready to merge.
merge_details: Merged by squash on 2026-03-02. Commit message: 'api: unify rate limit semantics and idempotency handling; OpenAI compat mappings' - merge method: squash
rollout_plan: Canary on hosted cluster in us-west-2 for 24h with 10% traffic
Monitor rate_limit_denied and idempotency_hit metrics and error_id spikes
If stable, increase to 100% over 6 hours and apply to Dedicated pools with opt-in config
Private installer will ship as opt-in config in next release; documented migration window of 28 days for OpenAI-compat headers
release_notes: Standardize Retry-After header on 429/503; Idempotency-Key now deduplicates repeated requests and allows safer retries for streaming when supported; OpenAI-compat layer now returns consistent error envelopes (type/message/param) and stable error_id for support; added observability metrics for rate limits and idempotency.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-1482: eviction alerts for idempotency store
ENG-1483: expand e2e matrix for SDK resume behavior across network failure modes
PM-322: update public SDK docs and changelog with migration guidance
testing_notes: Added unit + integration tests for rate-limit header shapes, idempotency replay correctness, and stream resume. Local resilience tests simulate mid-stream 503 and verify terminal error frame + Retry-After. CI flaky test retried once and passed; observed one transient on stream resume which is being tracked in ENG-1483.
notes_for_support: When customers report duplicate processing, ask for error_id from response; check idempotency_hit metric and dedup store for key. For clients seeing unexpected immediate 429 without Retry-After, confirm gateway version; during migration window old header shapes may still be returned for 28 days.
acknowledgements: Thanks to runtime team for streaming fixes and to observability for the new metrics and dashboards.
